summary: Akira Momiyama specializes in sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1972 to 1980 and held a professorship at Saitama University around 2004.

Akira Mukai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his doctoral course at Hokkaido University. He served as an assistant at Hokkaido University (attested 1978) and as a professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (attested 1999).

Akira Omine was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under Kyoshi Takahama and at Kyoto University and the University of Heidelberg, later holding professorships at Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Osaka University, and Ryukoku University.
Akira Onda worked in Buddhist studies and other fields. He served as a professor at Toyo University (attested 1974) and was later a professor emeritus at the University of Tokyo (attested 2002).

Akira Sadakata works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Hajime Nakamura, as well as at the University of Paris, later serving as associate professor and professor at Tokai University (~1971–2007).

Akira Saito specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Educated at the University of Tokyo under Jikido Takasaki and at the Australian National University, he held posts at Mie University, the University of Tokyo (2000–2016), and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Akira Shimada works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the College of Art, Delhi, under Rajeev Lochan and Daud Ali, and held positions at the British Museum and the State University of New York at New Paltz.

Akira Suganuma was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Toyo University, where he served as an assistant (~1962–1968) and associate professor (1991–1994), and also lectured at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (attested 1981).

Akira Takeda was a sinologist who completed his degrees at the University of Tokyo under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He taught at Tokyo Woman's Christian University (~1960–1970), served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (1965–1991), and was professor emeritus at Meikai University.
Akira Yamada was a philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Tokuryu Yamauchi from around 1943 to 1946. He later held a post at Nanzan University from around 1958 to 1967.

Akira Yuyama was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at ANU under J.W. de Jong and A.L. Basham, he held appointments at ANU, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and Soka University, among other institutions.

Akitoshi Saito is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held an academic career at Taisho University, where he was attested as a professor in 1982 and as professor emeritus in 2014.
Akong Tulku Rinpoche was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1967, he founded the Kagyu Samye Ling Monastery and Tibetan Centre, where he later served as abbot (attested 2009).

Akshay Ramanlal Desai worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He completed his studies at the University of Mumbai between approximately 1937 and 1946, studying under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye.

Alan Butterworth worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Elizabeth College and Balliol College, Oxford (~1883–1885), and served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1885 to 1918.

Alan Fox specializes in philosophy, sinology, and religious studies. After completing a PhD at Temple University (attested 1988), he held positions as professor (1992) and associate professor of philosophy (attested 2013–2014) at the University of Delaware.

Alan Gerard Wagner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2008) under Parimal G. Patil, having also studied under Robert M. Gimello, Charles Hallisey, Carl Bielefeldt, and Masatoshi Nagatomi.
Alan Gowans was a scholar in history, archaeology, and other fields. He completed his education at the University of Toronto in 1946 and at Princeton University in 1948 and 1950.

Alan John Bayard Wace was an archaeologist and historian educated at Shrewsbury School and Pembroke College under Robert Alexander Neil. He held posts at the British School at Athens, Victoria and Albert Museum, University of Cambridge, and Alexandria University.

Alan Lomax studied at St. Mark's School of Texas and Choate Rosemary Hall (~1929–1930) before attending Harvard University (~1932–1933), the University of Texas at Austin (~1933–1936), and Columbia University (~1939–1940).
